label: JZ Mock D · Paper 2 · Question 19
knowledgePattern: Group equivalent implications before enforcing a single true rule
solution:
Let P mean a>0 and Q mean f(a)>0. Statements 1 and 6 both say P⇒Q, while 4 is their contrapositive. These three always share a truth value, so none can be the sole truth.

Statement 2 says Q⇒P and 3 says ¬P⇒¬Q. These are contrapositives, excluding both as the sole truth.

Statement 7 says ¬Q⇔P. Its direction ¬Q⇒P is equivalent to ¬P⇒Q, which is statement 5. So 7 cannot be the sole truth either.

Statement 5 remains. It can indeed be the only true rule: take f(a)=1−a. It is positive whenever a≤0. Rules 1, 4 and 6 fail at a = 2; rules 2 and 3 fail at a = 0; rule 7 fails at a = 1/2. Answer E.

hints.title: Put each statement in if–then form
hints.body: Rewrite all seven statements as “If ..., then ...”. For “necessary and sufficient”, write both directions.
hints.recap: If P is sufficient for Q, write P implies Q. If P is necessary for Q, write Q implies P.
hints.pitfall: “P only if Q” puts Q after the arrow.
hints.pause: Translate every statement before comparing them.

recall.reminder: If P is sufficient for Q, write P implies Q. If P is necessary for Q, write Q implies P.

hints.title: Find statements that say the same thing
hints.body: Compare the arrows. Also compare each arrow with its contrapositive: “If P then Q” means the same as “If not Q then not P”.
hints.recap: Equivalent statements must be true or false together.
hints.pitfall: Negating a > 0 gives a ≤ 0, including zero.
hints.pause: Cross out any statement that would have to be true together with another.

recall.reminder: Equivalent statements must be true or false together.

hints.title: Check the two-way statement carefully
hints.body: Look at each direction of the necessary-and-sufficient statement separately. Does either direction force another statement on the list to be true?
hints.recap: A statement cannot be the only true one if it forces another to be true.
hints.pitfall: The reverse implication need not follow from a one-way implication.
hints.pause: Finish the eliminations and check that the remaining statement can stand alone.
